correctness.rationale: The proof identifies sigma classes as constant group-coordinate fibers with maxima at the top semilattice element; extracts unique G-invariant theta and normal N from every F-congruence; proves N must act trivially on the quotient; and constructs the converse quotient homomorphism. Flat-semiltattice meet identities exhaust the possible theta partitions, giving exact orbit/kernel counts. The faithful-transitive lattice is a direct order calculation. An independent closure-generated finite test checked cyclic degrees 2–4, a nontransitive action, nonabelian S3, and all Bell partitions in the eight-element boundary; no finite experiment is substituted for the general proof.

value.rationale: The complete F-congruence lattice of a natural infinite class of finite semilattice-by-group inverse monoids is determined, together with all quotient types and an exact orbit/kernel formula for any finite permutation action. Faithful-transitive rigidity collapses the entire proper quotient structure to two copies of the normal-subgroup lattice plus the identity; simple and symmetric groups then exhibit degree-independent counts five and seven. This answers a natural extension of an explicit published two-atom example and separates F-congruences sharply from ordinary congruences.
